_README: The script for this app's 'root is available, but not granted' video. Read by the shared scripts
in the `iboalali-apps` kit; see the `store-video` skill for the full shape and what each step verb
Nothing in this video is armed, mocked or captioned around. It is filmed on the BRC_api36_magisk
AVD, which has real Magisk in its ramdisk, so the refused state, the Superuser Request dialog and
the grant are all the real thing. That is the whole point: the state this video is about is the
one people write in about, and the fix is one prompt they have to be told to expect.
_locales: English only for now. Nothing here is a framework surface, so localeScope is 'app' and every
extra language is one caption set plus one `--locale <name>` run.
One caveat if a second language is ever added: Magisk's dialog follows the DEVICE locale, not
this app's, so it would stay English while the captions changed. The grant scene would need the
system locale set too, which on this AVD is possible because it is rootable.

_note: The promo's, unchanged. Taken from the launcher icon, which is the app's only real brand mark:
a white '#' on Material Deep Purple 500. See the promo storyboard for why it is deliberately
NOT the app's Material theme.

_zoom: The promo has no camera moves; this does, because its subject is a sentence rather than a green
tick. 'Root is available but this app has not been granted access' has to be read, and at the
size a phone-in-a-frame gives it, it is a grey smear.
The camera is wide for the Superuser Request dialog. It is centred and nearly full width, so at
2.0x the horizontal cut would crop its buttons off.

_package: The RELEASE build, unlike the promo and unlike howto/analytics. On a genuinely rooted device
nothing needs arming, so none of the debug tooling is wanted, and two things make release the
better choice rather than merely an acceptable one:
* Magisk's dialog names the package asking for root. A debug build would put
* There is no demo picker, no 'Demo:' menu row and no 'Debug: record products' card to hide,
because none of them is compiled in.
It needs keystore.properties present to sign. The test tags the journey drives are Compose
semantics properties, so they survive R8.
_device: Filmed on the BRC_api36_magisk AVD (real Magisk, google_apis, 1344x2992 at 480dpi, so the
pixel_9_pro_xl skin and all the geometry below are unchanged from the promo's).
Three one-time steps per boot, before recording. They are not in `shell` below because they
only need doing once and the last one restarts the framework:
for p in system vendor odm product system_ext bootimage; do \
That is what makes the device card read 'Pixel 9 Pro XL' and 'komodo' instead of 'emulator'
and 'emu64xa', which would contradict the Pixel bezel the capture is composited into. The
framework restart is required and is the reason resetprop alone does nothing: android.os.Build
is initialised in the zygote at boot, and every app inherits those values by forking from it.
The debug builds reach the same result with DemoDeviceOverride's launch extras. That path is
still the one for a device without root; this video does not need it.
_shell: Run before every pass. The journey grants this app root for real, and a grant that outlived
the pass would leave the take opening on an already-granted app, filming a different video
from the one that was rehearsed.
Needs a root shell, which is why `adb root` is in the per-boot steps above.

_note: The promo's bed. The same track across an app's videos is what makes them read as a set.
1300ms is a beat to read the device card before anything moves. The push goes to the
control about to be tapped, so the camera move and the press are one gesture.
2600ms because this is a real check against a real root implementation, which is slower
than the armed path the promo films.

caption.default:
Root is there,
but not allowed yet.

_note: The push onto the status area is the whole reason this video zooms. Two lines have to be
read: the message, and 'via Magisk' under it, which is what tells the viewer the app found
a manager and was refused by it rather than finding nothing.
A fixed focus point because the status text carries no tag and its wording is localized.
Magisk's own Superuser Request dialog, filmed rather than described. It records perfectly
well and answers an accessibility dump with nothing at all, so GRANT has no tag, no text
and no bounds to resolve: the tap is a fraction of the screen, which is the one place in
any of these storyboards where that is the right answer.
Re-measure the fraction from a screenshot if Magisk's dialog ever changes shape. Nothing
checks that the tap landed, so the failure mode is a video where nothing happens.

caption.default:
Now it can see
your root.

_note: The payoff, and the reason this is worth filming rather than captioning: the same screen
that said 'not granted' now reads 'Your Device has Root access', with the provider and its
version resolved through the grant that just happened.
The trailing wait is the tail the end card fades in over, and the recording is frozen on
its LAST frame for the whole hold.
The promo's card, unchanged. Same app, same offer, same link.
